I don't have write access to files in this environment (no Edit/Write tool), and this repo is currently empty — no `controlled-items.md`, `verification.md`, `ship.md`, or PR #482 diff/eval report for me to read. So I can draft the record as text below, but I can't independently verify several of your claims, and I want to flag that before you file this as "known-good."

**Two things worth resolving before this gets locked in as a rollback baseline:**

1. **I can't see PR #482 or the eval results directly.** Everything below about scope and eval numbers is based on your description, not verified evidence. If you can point me at the PR diff and the eval report (paste them, or tell me where they live in the repo), I'll fold in actual numbers/links instead of placeholders.
2. **Embedding model swaps often aren't cleanly revertible by code rollback alone.** If `embed-v2` outputs are being written into a vector index/cache/store, rolling back the *code* to v2.2.x won't restore known-good behavior unless the v1 embeddings/index are also still intact and re-activated. Worth confirming explicitly, since this is the exact thing a "what can we roll back to" record needs to get right — otherwise the baseline is misleading.

This also touches production-facing recommendation quality for real users, so I'd treat it as more than a routine dependency bump — worth a second pair of eyes (whoever owns the recommendation service) rather than just this doc.
